races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sole Ruler
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has finished 7th and 4th on Good ground, meaning he carries the heaviest burden in this setup — needing a strong pace from The Mean Fiddler that simply may not materialise; Paul Mulrennan has strong course claims but the tactical position is uncomfortable with 43 days between runs.|

runners_data.name: Reflect On Glory
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is in sharp form (10/42 over 14 days) and this lightly raced filly showed a placed effort at 6f on Good last time, making her one to respect on upside; her style is unclassified, and being lightly raced means she could improve significantly here, though she arrives as one of the closers needing the pace to honest up.|

runners_data.name: The Mean Fiddler
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field, stepping from 5f to 6f with a placed effort on Good ground and now able to control every aspect of the race — the tongue-tie is noted and bears watching, but Jason Hart's handling of the tactics will be the defining factor; uncontested lead on a flat 6f at Ripon is a significant physical and tactical advantage.|

runners_data.name: War Gaming
runners_data.note: Wearing blinkers for the first time after a 2nd and 3rd on Good ground at 5f and 6f respectively, War Gaming is the most experienced horse in the field by results and is likely to press The Mean Fiddler from a prominent pitch; Cieren Fallon's booking adds confidence, but the blinkers suggest connections are asking him to be sharper from the gate rather than stalking.|

races.paceDynamic: The Mean Fiddler is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no challenger for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, self-regulated tempo over Ripon's flat 6f. War Gaming will press from a prominent position, but with only four runners and no pace battle brewing, The Mean Fiddler can control the fractions entirely on his own terms. Reflect On Glory and Sole Ruler will be shuffled back into rear positions, giving them ground to make up against a leader likely to get an easy, energy-conserving first half. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent types who can control the race from the front and resist any late charge — lone front-runners operating at a sustainable clip on Good ground at Ripon are precisely the profile to exploit this setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler leads unchallenged and sets a measured, honest pace that saps the closers' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: The Mean Fiddler dictates from flag to finish on Good ground, his 5f experience translating well stepping up to 6f with extra time to conserve energy; War Gaming, pressed close throughout, is best placed to challenge if the leader weakens but is racing from behind the front-runner's tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler sets a pace that proves faster than it looks and ties up inside the final furlong, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Sole Ruler, dropping back from rear, or Reflect On Glory arriving from midfield could benefit if the early fractions prove misleading and the field strings out; this relies on the front-runner overcooking it despite having no rival to force the pace, which is an unlikely but not impossible outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If War Gaming actively challenges The Mean Fiddler early and turns this into a genuine contested lead.
scenarios.body: A pace duel between The Mean Fiddler and War Gaming would compress the time advantage for the closers and open the door for Reflect On Glory or Sole Ruler to pick up the pieces; however, War Gaming's form suggests he is content to race prominently rather than seize the lead aggressively, making a genuine duel unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler crawls to set up a pure sprint, turning the race into a dash over the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace compresses the field and negates positional advantage, giving every runner an equal chance in a sprint finish; Reflect On Glory, lightly raced and potentially unexposed, could thrive in this scenario, while War Gaming's blinkers suggest he needs to be engaged rather than waiting for a late dash.

watchPoints.text: Watch The Mean Fiddler's early fractions — if Jason Hart sets an unusually slow tempo, the race morphs into a sprint and his positional advantage is neutralised, opening the door to every runner equally.

War Gaming's first-time blinkers are a significant unknown — if they sharpen him enough to challenge The Mean Fiddler for the lead early, it could transform the race shape entirely and benefit the closers.
Sole Ruler's 43-day absence means fitness cannot be assumed; if he is not fully wound up, his hold-up style at the rear of a small, slowly-run field leaves him with nowhere to hide.

Reflect On Glory's lightly raced status (just one run) means any significant improvement from that 3rd-place debut at 6f on Good could make her competitive regardless of the pace shape — Burke's yard form makes her the most live unknown in the race.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster filly with a consistent placed record at 5f and 6f on good ground, running in form (0W3P from similar conditions) — she is genuinely a prominent-racing type but the three-way contest for early position means she may not get as clean a berth as she wants.

runners_data.name: Rohini
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's South African-trained runner has a grim UK record (five runs, all 7th or 8th), and while she is a natural hold-up type that tag is partly a consequence of redistribution — she has barely threatened even from her preferred position and the step up in class is no help.

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's four-year-old has shown a consistent tendency to fade in the closing stages across 15 runs on similar ground, and a 49-day absence does nothing to inspire confidence about her finishing effort over 6f.

runners_data.name: All Good
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's filly returns after 293 days off the track with only two runs on soft/standard ground to her name — the step to good turf over 6f is unknown territory, and the trainer's recent strike rate of 0 from 17 over 14 days tempers expectations despite the decent OR.

runners_data.name: Royale Union
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly steps back from 7f to 6f which could sharpen her, and the trainer fires in winners at 10/42 over 14 days; Clifford Lee takes over in the saddle and the good ground form (0W1P) is at least consistent with conditions, though she is untested at this trip.

runners_data.name: Secret Harvest
runners_data.note: Conrad Allen's filly finished a clear second on her most recent start at this course and distance on good ground, confirming both her front-running style and her affinity for these exact conditions — the jockey booking of Cieren Fallon is a positive, though the trainer's 14-day record is quiet at 0/3.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Harvest is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to push her hard from the gates, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Ripon's straight 6f on good ground. Queen Sana and Royale Union are both prominent types who will want to race close to the pace, meaning the early portions of this race will see at least three horses jostling for position in the first two furlongs before order is established. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate cleanly — Queen Sana and Royale Union are both genuine front-runners or prominent racers, but Secret Harvest is most likely to secure the lead given her confirmed style, with Queen Sana and Royale Union settling just off her in the first two positions. A steady-to-honest pace set by Secret Harvest on good turf strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final furlong, making the prominent and pace-pressing profile the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Secret Harvest Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Harvest leads uncontested at a fair clip and the prominent horses behind her cannot sustain their effort to the line.
scenarios.body: Secret Harvest bowls along at the head of affairs and the even gallop on good ground plays to those capable of racing close to the pace without exhausting themselves early; horses who travel prominently and quicken from that position have the clearest path.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Sana or Royale Union press Secret Harvest hard from the outset, lifting the tempo and forcing a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: An elevated pace burns off Secret Harvest in the final furlong and rewards any runner with a stronger finish from just off the pace; Royale Union's step back in trip from 7f could prove an advantage if she settles just behind a pressured leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot and the front three tie each other up, leaving a window for a closer to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: All Good or Aurora's Doublesix would need to overcome their modest recent form and Aurora's habitual fade, so this scenario is structurally possible but undermined by the redistribution of true hold-up types and Aurora's consistent finishing weakness.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Harvest misses the break or is collected early and no horse takes control, producing a messy tactical crawl.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race over 6f on good ground would compress the field and turn the finish into a sprint lottery; in that context any horse capable of producing a sharp burst off a slow tempo could theoretically get involved, but the low-class hold-up runners lack the raw ability to capitalise reliably.

watchPoints.text: Secret Harvest — watch whether Cieren Fallon commits to the lead immediately from the gates; if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged through the first two furlongs, her course-and-distance second on good ground becomes a serious live form line.

Queen Sana and Royale Union — both want to race prominently and will be pressing for the same ground in the first furlong; a bump or check early could unsettle either filly and distort the pace map entirely.

All Good — 293 days off the track for Julie Camacho whose stable is out of form over the last fortnight; watch the market closely for any meaningful support that might suggest the gallops have told a different story.

Aurora's Doublesix — her repeated fade pattern flags her as a horse to oppose rather than follow; if she appears to travel well into the race, expect the fade to kick in from the 2f pole as it has done consistently across her record.

races.name: Weatherbys Bloodstock Pro Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained front-runner wearing headgear, Cieren Fallon booked; she must battle Zoustar Dreams for the lead from flag-fall, and her inconsistent recent form (two seventh places in last four) raises questions about her ability to front-run cleanly under pressure at 5f on good ground.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old is the most course-and-distance experienced runner in the field with nine runs over 5f on good ground and two wins from those; races prominently and likely to find the contested pace suits her well as she tracks the leaders and challenges through the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's hold-up filly has won over this exact trip and course on good ground most recently and is in the best current form of her career; her late-running style makes her the natural beneficiary if the front two set a strong early gallop, and James Sullivan is an experienced handler of this type of tactical race.

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 3-year-old arrives with three wins in her last four outings and is a confirmed front-runner who wears headgear; she has the strongest recent form of any runner here and her 5f good-ground record is solid, but she will face immediate pressure from Creative Queen and her task is harder than in her recent straightforward victories.

runners_data.name: North West Gal
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's filly returns after a lengthy 67-day absence and her best form has come on softer or standard ground rather than good; she races prominently and is capable of placing but the layoff and going combination introduce meaningful fitness and ground uncertainty heading into a race that may be run too quickly for her.

races.paceDynamic: Creative Queen and Zoustar Dreams are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the off over this sharp 5f at Ripon, creating a genuinely contested early gallop that is unlikely to relent on this good ground. Creative Queen wears headgear and has Cieren Fallon in the saddle for the powerful Haggas yard, while Zoustar Dreams arrives in flying form having won three of her last four and will not be willing to sit off the pace. The result will be a high-tempo, honest race from the front that burns through the early fractions and sets up a test of stamina in the closing stages. This race shape clearly favours off-the-pace profiles — specifically hold-up and patient midfield types who can exploit the leaders emptying themselves — with Angel Numbers the obvious beneficiary given her strong recent form from off the pace at this exact course and distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Battle, Closer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Creative Queen and Zoustar Dreams fight for supremacy and burn each other out inside the opening two furlongs, leaving the race wide open for a late challenge.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace sets a searingly honest tempo that depletes both front-runners before the final furlong, rewarding a hold-up horse who can swoop late. Angel Numbers, who won over this exact course and distance on good ground and races from well off the pace, is perfectly profiled to capitalise as the leaders tie up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Zoustar Dreams Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Zoustar Dreams asserts early dominance and Creative Queen fails to match her stride, allowing Zoustar Dreams to dictate a controlled, moderate tempo.
scenarios.body: With clean air and a steady pace to herself, Zoustar Dreams can conserve energy through the race and produce a strong final furlong from a position of comfort — her three recent wins have all come when allowed to race on her own terms. Marajito, tracking prominently, is the most likely to chase her down if she does not get it all her own way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, All Flat
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle between the two front-runners is fiercer than anticipated and all horses meet the rising ground at Ripon's finish on empty tanks.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a desperate scramble in the final 100 yards with no clear winner pulling clear, compressing the field and making positional luck around the rail crucial. North West Gal, who has placed prominently and arrives fresh off a 67-day break, may find the conditions drawing her back into contention if she handles the return well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Creative Queen Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Creative Queen, aided by her headgear and Cieren Fallon's forcing tactics, immediately establishes a clear lead and is never seriously challenged.
scenarios.body: Running at a regulated pace of her own choosing, Creative Queen would have every chance of turning this into a test of her best qualities — she has won on soft and placed on good and has the class of the Haggas yard behind her. However, her recent form figures of 6-2-1-7-7 are inconsistent and this scenario depends on Zoustar Dreams failing to fire, making it the least probable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Creative Queen and Zoustar Dreams — watch the first furlong closely; if both go hard immediately, the pace will be fierce enough to compromise both their finishing efforts and the race will be gifted to the back markers.

Angel Numbers — if she fails to get a clear run or is shuffled back further than ideal in a field of only five, her late challenge may come too late on this sharp 5f track that offers limited room to make up ground.

Zoustar Dreams — her trainer T14 strike rate of 1/15 is modest and this will be her first time racing against another confirmed front-runner; monitor how Jack Callan (3lb claimer) handles the early tactical battle.

North West Gal — 67 days off the track is notable and her best ground has been softer than today's good; watch her in the paddock for any signs of well-being before assessing her claims on returning from a break.

Marajito — her nine runs at 5f on good ground (2W2P from those) make her quietly the most consistent performer at this exact level; watch whether she can track the pace war closely enough to pounce if both leaders fade simultaneously.

races.name: Wilmot-smith Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D in Good ground recently and holds a solid place record at the track; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a practical weight relief and the 14-day turnaround following a sixth suggests a freshened horse; prominent style suits this pace map ideally.

runners_data.name: Saint Lawrence
runners_data.note: Shane Gray takes the ride on this well-travelled 8-year-old who has a second at course and distance in Good going within recent form; wear of a hood (hg:b) may help focus, but the 17-day break and a string of modest finishes temper expectations, and his natural hold-up style is not perfectly served by an uncontested front-runner.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and highest-rated horse in the field at OR 94; won over this C&D in Good going and Tudhope is a strong partner, but the visor (hg:v) and style-fit flag of 0.93 suggest he is catalogued here slightly out of ideal positional role — his chance is real but the flag signals a mild discount in races requiring reactive pace work.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with four placed efforts from twelve runs in Good ground and consecutive second-place finishes in his last two starts over 6f; Connor Beasley knows the horse well, the prominent style fits the expected race shape, though a zero-win sequence and a tendency to finish second rather than first is noted.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, though the saturated rear of this field means he is unlikely to find his true rearward berth and is effectively racing out of role; four-from-six blank finishes in 2024 and a style-fit flag of 0.92 both temper confidence, and his 0W1P record in similar going is slim.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Tim Easterby's yard with a form string of four consecutive unplaced runs and a modest 0W3P record in similar going; hold-up style is natural but the map has him out of his best position, and the young horse's consistency issues make him hard to trust in a race with a compressed early order.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley has drawn a blank in the past 21 days (T14:0/21) and this 7-year-old's recent form reads three consecutive zeros; his hold-up tendency is genuine but, placed into midfield by redistribution, he races away from his strongest ground, and the finish-fading flag combined with a 0W1P record in similar conditions makes him a difficult proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Dark Cloud Rising is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger prepared to press from outside, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Lord Roxby and Commanche Falls are both prominent types who will track closely behind, creating a compressed early order with three horses effectively racing in formation across the first three furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can genuinely accommodate at the rear — Rousing Encore and Grant Wood are true come-from-behind horses redistributed into midfield slots because the pace map is saturated at that end, meaning neither is likely to achieve a truly rearward, ground-saving position. With an uncontested, metronomic gallop expected on Good ground over six furlongs at Ripon — a track that does not brutally punish front-runners — this shape firmly favours horses racing prominently who can be produced with a single clean effort in the final two furlongs, rather than those relying on a strong pace collapse to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse racing in the first three.
scenarios.body: Dark Cloud Rising dictates from the front and, without pressure, keeps the tempo honest enough to hold on or hand the advantage to Lord Roxby or Commanche Falls who track directly behind and pounce in the closing stages; the compressed early order means no late acceleration gap opens for hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Nails It
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just honest enough to set up a winning challenge from a horse creeping into contention from fourth or fifth.
scenarios.body: Saint Lawrence, despite usually holding-up, has course form and may find a rhythm close enough to the pace to benefit if the front two tire marginally in the final furlong; the Good ground suits and a sharp track finish at Ripon can reward a horse angled wide with momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves deceptively fast and the front-runners tie up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the scenario that would theoretically suit Rousing Encore or Boston Dan coming from off the pace, but both are mapped out of their truest hold-up position and Boston Dan's recent form string of consecutive zeros gives little confidence in a late rattle; even if the pace does collapse, the redistribution of hold-up horses means the most-suited types are not ideally placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising meets no interference, is allowed to bowl along at its own rhythm, and simply outstays the field.
scenarios.body: Dark Cloud Rising showed a win over this course and distance in Good ground and carries the highest OR in the field; if the prominent trackers are unable to close the gap through the final two furlongs, the front-runner simply holds on under Tudhope's patient waiting tactics.

watchPoints.text: Dark Cloud Rising setting an uncontested, slow early gallop is the single biggest shape risk — if Tudhope rolls along unchallenged, the race may never develop a true pace and prominent trackers Lord Roxby and Commanche Falls need to judge when to commit.

Commanche Falls has finished second in back-to-back starts but has not won in this entire form cycle; watch whether Connor Beasley opts to challenge early or times a late run, as the horse's tendency to get touched off suggests it needs to be produced later than instinct suggests.

Rousing Encore and Grant Wood are both true hold-up horses mapped into midfield — if they are unable to find gaps coming off a sustained gallop and are squeezed for room in a seven-runner field on a straight six furlongs, they risk finishing without ever landing a meaningful blow.

Lord Roxby's Alex Jary 3lb claim brings his carried weight to a competitive level relative to the field; watch market confidence on this combination as Nigel Tinkler has the horse freshened off a 14-day break following a poor run, and a bounce-back is structurally plausible.

Grant Wood is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — on Good ground over 6f at Ripon with a flat track and a steady gallop, any tendency to idle or shorten stride late will be fully exposed; his OR of 77 is the lowest in the field and the redistribution out of his natural position compounds the concern.

races.name: North Yorkshire Ice Cream Championship 2026 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey's 4yo has won over 10f on Good ground and arrives in excellent recent form (3-2-1 last three), and will travel prominently just off Poet's Dawn, making it ideally placed to capitalise if the leader tires — the 16-day turnaround looks sharp and Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is a useful weight concession.|

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up operator has recorded a win and two places over 10f on Good ground but must wait for others to do the donkey work, and with only a crawl likely behind an uncontested leader the closing ground may not materialise; 29 days off is not a concern for this yard, but the race shape is the primary obstacle.|

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: 284 days off the track is the dominant concern for Tina Jackson's 5yo despite Clifford Lee in the saddle, and while the horse has strong placed form over 10-12f in Good conditions (three placings from 11 runs), a horse returning from that layoff against in-form rivals at this distance needs to be taken on trust; the trainer's 1/5 in 14 days shows horses are fit.|

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 4yo won over 8f on Good ground and has placed over 10-12f in similar conditions, but as a hold-up type relying on Poet's Dawn to force an honest pace, it is dependent on a tempo it cannot manufacture itself; only 8 days between runs suggests a horse in a purple patch, and Jason Hart is an asset if a late run is ever on.|

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 11-year-old has an outstanding record in similar conditions (11/15, 4W5P) and arrives just four days after its last run with headgear worn — this is a trainer who targets this horse at specific opportunities, and an uncontested lead at Ripon on Good ground over 10f is precisely the scenario that suits it best.|

races.paceDynamic: Poet's Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 1m2f handicap at Ripon and, with no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the outset. Everyoneknowsadave and His Finest Hour will press forward into prominent positions just off the pace, meaning the field is likely to compress into a tight bunch behind Poet's Dawn rather than string out. With Good ground, a flat track, and a single pace-setter allowed a free lead, the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching — Poet's Dawn can nurse the field through the middle stages and control the race's rhythm entirely. This shape strongly favours front-running and prominently-ridden horses, as the absence of early pressure reduces the premium on finishing pace and rewards those closest to a leader who controls their own fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn Controls Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn leads unchallenged throughout and the pace stays honest-but-comfortable, the front-runner converts a controlled tempo into an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: Poet's Dawn dictates every yard on Good ground where it has a 4W5P record in similar conditions, leaving pursuers chasing a moving target into the final furlong at Ripon's flat finish; an 11-year-old with this course profile rarely wastes a free lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Everyoneknowsadave or His Finest Hour close up early and time a challenge to sweep past Poet's Dawn inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Both prominent types have recent placed form at 10f on Good ground and would relish a target to aim at late; Everyoneknowsadave in particular has won over this trip in similar conditions and carries strong recent form (321 last three).

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong and the front two tire, allowing Mao Shang Wong or Polygram to pick up ground from off the pace in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mao Shang Wong has winning form over 10f on Good ground and O'Meara's yard is 5/56 over 14 days suggesting horses are returning to form; Polygram showed a win over 8f on Good and has place claims if the leaders set it up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn misses the break or is checked early, disrupting the expected race shape entirely and forcing a muddled, slow-run affair.
scenarios.body: Without a reliable pace-setter this becomes a tactical lottery where any of the field could win, though His Finest Hour's jumper-style stamina at 12f and Polygram's course-form over Good ground give both residual each-way claims.

watchPoints.text: Poet's Dawn wears headgear (hg:p) and runs just four days after its last start — watch the market to confirm Easterby has this horse primed for today, as any early market drift may signal the short turnaround has caught up with an 11-year-old.

Everyoneknowsadave and His Finest Hour are both prominent-style runners who will want to press forward early — if they both commit aggressively for the same ground behind Poet's Dawn, early jostling could disrupt the shape and bring the hold-up horses unexpectedly into play.

His Finest Hour returns from 284 days off the track; watch how it handles the preliminary paddock assessment and whether Clifford Lee gives it an educational or a competitive ride — a horse this fresh can either run big first time out or need the race.

Mao Shang Wong's chance is almost entirely pace-dependent — watch early sectionals to see whether Poet's Dawn sets a genuine tempo; if the gallop is very slow, Conor Whiteley may be forced to improve his position earlier than ideal, undermining the hold-up profile.

Ripon's flat 1m2f track with Good ground suits a front-runner who can control fractions — watch where Poet's Dawn settles in the early stages; if it is allowed a three-length advantage by halfway, the race may effectively be over before the home turn.

races.name: Queen Ethelburga's Collegiate Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dacres Cross
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up operator has shown consistent form on good ground (10 sim-going runs, 1 win, 2 places) and steps up to a mile which should suit given 7f form; naturally races from the rear but the compressed pace map means finding clear air late may prove the main obstacle.

runners_data.name: Vega's Virtue
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's mare carries a headgear (hood) and brings the strongest recent profile in the race — two wins at 8f on good ground in her last nine starts and a 16-day turnaround for a yard with a 3/87 recent strike; races from off the pace and will need the tempo to ensure her strong closing style registers.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner has gone winless in 6 good-ground starts and the form string reads six without a placed effort; genuinely a hold-up horse forced into a midfield slot by the congestion of closers here, and his fair-weather sim-going record (3/6) is not encouraging against better types.

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls sends this one here having faded in finish in recent starts — a consistent pattern of dropping away late — and his true hold-up style sits uncomfortably in a race with one pace-setter; a single sim-going placing in five attempts compounds the concern, making this scenario-dependent at best.

runners_data.name: Tago Mago
runners_data.note: Sam England's lightly-raced three-year-old steps back to a trip shorter than his last two (both 7f at Southwell) and the only turf run on good ground produced a creditable third; a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the map, but relatively unexposed and Oisin Orr in the saddle is an upgrade.

runners_data.name: Amber Hamur
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's confirmed pace-setter has won and been placed multiple times at 8f on good ground and the uncontested lead here is hers for the taking; Connor Beasley rides and the combination of sole front-runner status, a positive trainer-14-day record (5/28), and a course-appropriate flat track makes this the race to set the tactical agenda.

runners_data.name: Hey Havana
runners_data.note: Geoffrey Harker's mare repeatedly runs well at this trip and going — seven runs on good ground producing five placings or better — and her prominent style puts her in the slipstream of Amber Hamur from the outset; the trainer's recent record is modest (0/3) but the horse's consistency at this level is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Itszaboy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's runner holds the lowest OR in the race (52) and his form string shows six efforts without a placing on good ground across his last six starts; a hold-up horse relocated into midfield by the busy back-end of this field, the style-fit concern and weakest rating in the race make this a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Amber Hamur is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Hey Havana the only other prominent-type in the field, she is virtually guaranteed a clear lead at her own tempo over this flat Ripon mile on good ground. That amounts to a controlled, unchallenged gallop through the early stages — enough pace to string the field out but not enough to set up a truly searching test that would play into the hands of late closers. The field is packed with hold-up horses: Sailor's Return, Scheffler, Tago Mago, Itszaboy, Dacres Cross, and Vega's Virtue all want to come from off the pace, but with only one genuine pace-setter the race may not generate sufficient tempo to allow all of them to close effectively. This race shape strongly favours Amber Hamur and Hey Havana — horses at the front and prominent end who avoid traffic, save ground, and are not reliant on a fast pace being set for them. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear; of those, Vega's Virtue and Dacres Cross are the most likely to slot into a tractable midfield position and get a run, while the deeper hold-up types face a more congested and pace-starved scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amber Hamur Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Hamur leads unchallenged at a fair, controlled tempo and Hey Havana settles just behind in a clear second position.
scenarios.body: Amber Hamur rolls along with no rival willing to commit to pressing her, meaning she controls both the pace and the ground, turning for home with the race at her mercy; horses reliant on a strong gallop to close into find the pace insufficient and meet a wall of traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana pushes forward to challenge Amber Hamur early and a genuine duel develops through the middle part of the race.
scenarios.body: The pressure between two front-runners quickens the pace enough to catch Amber Hamur late but still not enough to fully unlock the back-markers; Hey Havana, racing in her comfort zone at a track where she has run into the frame repeatedly, is best placed to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to compress finishing times and the closers get a clear run through on the good ground.
scenarios.body: Vega's Virtue is the best-credentialled hold-up type here with two wins on good ground at this trip and a positive trainer-strike-rate; Dacres Cross also has course form to deploy but the restricted pace makes a full close from the rear unlikely for most of this group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Hamur sets only a crawl and the entire field concertinas behind her turning into the straight.
scenarios.body: A steadily-run race on flat Ripon ground produces a sprint finish where positional luck and a sharp turn of foot matter more than tactical nous; Scheffler's redistribution out of natural hold-up role means it is poorly placed for this, while Tago Mago showed a useful third last time and could emerge from a messy pack.

watchPoints.text: Amber Hamur leads unbothered from flag — watch whether Connor Beasley uses that solo lead to dictate or gives away the advantage by going too slowly, as either extreme changes the shape materially.

Vega's Virtue is the most dangerous hold-up horse in the field; watch how quickly Duran Fentiman moves her into contention around the home turn, as leaving it too late on a flat track with a slow pace could cost her the race.

Hey Havana has been placed at this course and trip multiple times — watch her positioning in the early stages; if she elects to press Amber Hamur rather than track her, the pace scenario changes from Scenario A to Scenario B immediately.

Sailor's Return and Scheffler are both genuine hold-up types mapped into midfield — watch whether either jockey makes an early decision to push forward, as doing so would be racing against their horse's natural style and could compromise their chance regardless of outcome.

Tago Mago is lightly raced with only three career runs and is stepping onto turf at a shorter trip — watch the market for any significant move, as unexposed horses with Oisin Orr booked can outperform their nominal hold-up slot at short odds in modest handicaps.
